title: Complement-quadric duality: e2=0 on an a-subset <=> its (n-a)-complement satisfies S^2=-Q quadric point count (Weil right tool)
evidence: Probes scripts/probes/_407_conn/C082_quadric_pointcount.py and C082_variance_mechanism.py (exact integer arithmetic, proper dyadic subgroups mu_n, n=8/16/32/64, large primes q=1 mod n with q>>n, multiple primes per n). RESULTS: (A) The duality identity itself is correct -- the in-tree Lean theorem ComplementQuadric.e2Folded_eq_zero_iff_complement_quadric is axiom-clean [propext,Classical.choice,Quot.sound], and my probe re-verifies e2(A)=0 <=> complement-quadric S_T^2=-Q_T 8/8 on random A at every prime. So the structural flip (top rows -> complement-quadric form) is genuine. (B) DECISIVE: the bad-complement count by c=|T| splits cleanly. c=1,2: count=0 (forced -- 2*g^{2i}=0 impossible). c=3: count = EXACTLY n at every n (8->8,16->16,32->32,64->64) and q-INDEPENDENT across all 4 primes per n. These very-top rows are the 'fully coset-decomposable' ones the record cites -- but the q-independence comes from the FORCED symmetric-function vanishing (e1=e2=0 on mu_n is automatic, the F15/SubsetSumEsymmVanishing identity), a CLOSED root-of-unity identity, NOT from classical quadric/Weil theory. (C) From c=4 onward (a=n-4 and deeper) the count VARIES across primes with the same n: at n=32 the c=4 count is 40,40,40,72,72,40,40,40 over 8 primes; c=5 is 64,96,0,0. The variance is generator-INDEPENDENT (identical over 5 distinct primitive roots g per prime -> a genuine subgroup invariant, not an artifact). (D) The 'Weil is the right tool' premise is structurally wrong: a classical FREE-variable nondegenerate c-variable quadric S^2=-Q over F_q^c has point count ~ q^{c-1} (q-DEPENDENT, ~1.5e9 at c=4); the actual mu_n-restricted count is ~20, ratio ~1e-8. The object is a mu_n-RESTRICTED (partial / incomplete) sum, NOT a full-field quadric, so classical quadratic-form/Weil theory computes the wrong object by ~q^{c-1}.
wall: BGK / Paley (partial subgroup character-sum wall). The c>=4 complement-quadric count = #{c-subsets of mu_n carrying an additive relation S^2=-Q beyond the forced e1=e2=0}, a mu_n-restricted incomplete sum whose value depends on accidental ±1 relations among 2^mu-th roots mod the specific prime q -- prime-dependent at fixed n. This is exactly the partial-subgroup quadratic Gauss sum already isolated as the open gap in DISPROOF_LOG O22/O23 (Rounds 6-7): the full-field->subgroup bridge needs Weil-on-curves, which is the same deep-moment / additive-energy CRUX as faces 3<->4 of the open core.
honest_note: The connection's Lean identity is real and axiom-clean, and the structural insight (high-agreement rows = low-dimension complement-quadric geometry) is legitimately useful as a reformulation. What is REFUTED is only the operative hope -- that small fixed dimension lets classical Weil/Deligne give an exact q-independent delta* on the top rows independent of BGK. The probe shows the q-independent rows (c<=3) carry no new delta* content beyond the existing coset/F15 census, while the first row with genuine content (c=4 = agreement a=n-4) is already prime-arithmetic-dependent = the BGK wall. 'Small fixed dimension dodges the dimension obstruction' is false: the dimension IS small but the variables are constrained to mu_n, making the object a partial sum -- precisely the obstruction Weil-for-full-quadrics does not address. NOT a closure; the core remains the 25-year-open partial-subgroup character-sum/BGK wall. This c>=4 variance finding should be logged to DISPROOF_LOG as the concrete falsification of the 'Weil-right-tool' premise (a sharpening of the existing O22/O23 partial-sum no-go via an explicit prime-dependent point-count). Probe time-boxed; not Lean-formalized (the conclusion is a refutation of an informal premise, not a clean isolated lemma).
